name: Citizenship by Naturalisation

requirements.blocker_text: 5 years' permanent residence in Mongolia (Law on Citizenship 1995, Article 9.1).
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 5 years on the G (immigrant) permanent-residence status.

requirements.blocker_text: Proper knowledge of the Mongolian language and of Mongolian people's traditions and customs.
Suitable living capability and resources: monthly income at least 10 times the minimum wage.
Must not have committed crimes during the residency period, and foreign relations must not prejudice Mongolia's interests.
Must renounce prior citizenship, unless the applicant's country of origin prohibits renunciation (Law on Citizenship, Article 4.2).
The President may waive the standard Article 9.1 conditions for individuals with exceptional talents or achievements that benefit Mongolia.

evidence_required.document: Character/background certificate from country of residence or its diplomatic mission
Proof of renunciation of prior citizenship, or its impossibility

sources.title: Immigration Agency of Mongolia -- citizenship by naturalisation: 5 years' permanent residence, income at least 10x minimum wage, Mongolian language/customs/constitutional knowledge, clean background certificate from country of residence or its diplomatic mission; 6 months to 1 year processing, 60,000 MNT fee

ecoi.net (Austrian Red Cross/ACCORD country-of-origin information network) -- Law of Mongolia on Citizenship, 5 June 1995, English translation: Article 9 naturalisation conditions, Article 4 dual-citizenship prohibition and renunciation exception, Article 9.3 Presidential waiver for exceptional talent

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Mongolia). STATUS: DRAFT -- the core Article 9 conditions (residence, language/customs, income, no-crimes) are corroborated by a tier-1 Immigration Agency page, but the renunciation and Presidential-waiver clauses (Articles 4.2, 9.3) are sourced only to a tier-2 full-text translation of the 1995 Law on Citizenship (ecoi.net, an established European country-of-origin-information network, treated as tier-2 in this dataset's convention consistent with Refworld) -- since this dataset requires ALL hard requirements to be tier-1 for published status, and two of this route's hard requirements are tier-2-only, the file stays draft rather than published despite the strong overall sourcing. dual_citizenship_allowed is FALSE -- Article 4.1 explicitly prohibits Mongolian citizens from holding another nationality simultaneously, one of the stricter dual-citizenship bans in this dataset (contrast Israel's and Romania's permissive stance). NO MARRIAGE-BASED FAST TRACK exists -- Article 3.3 explicitly states marriage does not itself change citizenship, and no reduced-residence marriage provision was found anywhere in the fetched text, a genuine structural absence (see mn_family_reunification.json).
